metadata.blurb: OKX Wallet is a universal crypto wallet available on multiple platforms, including app, web, and extension

ref.explanation: OKX says OKX Wallet has taken the lead in supporting Ethereum's EIP-7702 account-abstraction standard.
OKX's wallet setup guide documents creating a wallet with a seed phrase and importing an existing wallet using a seed phrase or private key.
OKX says OKX Wallet integrates ENS, allowing users to send, receive, and display assets using a .eth domain.
OKX says OKX Wallet integrates ENS, allowing users to send, receive, and display assets using a .eth domain.
OKX's help center documents entering Wallet > Trade > Swap > Bridge to make cross-chain transfers through OKX DEX.

OKX says the wallet dashboard tracks multi-chain, multi-wallet, and multi-asset holdings, asset allocation, DeFi portfolios/liabilities/earnings, approvals, and transaction history across multiple networks.

OKX says the wallet dashboard tracks multi-chain, multi-wallet, and multi-asset holdings, asset allocation, DeFi portfolios/liabilities/earnings, approvals, and transaction history across multiple networks.

OKX says the wallet dashboard tracks multi-chain, multi-wallet, and multi-asset holdings, asset allocation, DeFi portfolios/liabilities/earnings, approvals, and transaction history across multiple networks.
OKX documents adding a custom RPC endpoint in OKX Wallet on both the app and web extension; users enter network name, RPC URL, chain ID, currency symbol, and optional explorer URL.
OKX developer documentation describes the injected provider API used by dApps to request accounts and signing through OKX Wallet, and OKX's EIP-6963 article lists OKX Wallet as supporting EIP-6963.
OKX's EIP-7702 article describes account-abstraction support and batched/automated smart-account capabilities; the exact delegation contract remains unknown.
The OKX Wallet App Store privacy label lists Diagnostics / Crash Data, Performance Data, and Other Diagnostic Data as collected but not linked to identity.
The OKX Wallet App Store privacy label lists Usage Data / Product Interaction and Other Usage Data for analytics and app functionality.
The OKG Bug Bounty Program enlists the help of the hacker community at HackerOne to make OKG more secure.
Policy includes a Safe Harbor: compliant research is authorized and OKG says it will not initiate legal action.
OKX wallet settings let users choose the wallet authentication method, including biometrics or password, and OKX wallet setup also offers Face ID or fingerprint login depending on device support.
OKX publishes a step-by-step guide for connecting Keystone hardware wallets to the OKX app and OKX Wallet browser extension, including send/receive/swap features.

OKX Wallet documentation defines RPC as the protocol the wallet uses to communicate with blockchain networks and documents adding HTTPS custom RPC endpoints, indicating RPC-backed operation rather than an embedded Ethereum L1 light client.
OKX says its approval-management upgrade filters malicious approval poisoning linked to wallet addresses.
OKX says its second line of defense automatically blocks and prompts users to review transaction risks for potentially risky DApp requests, including phishing-link scenarios.
OKX Wallet security materials say the wallet scans addresses, identifies malicious addresses, and blocks interaction with malicious DApps or addresses.

OKX Wallet says its high-risk transaction interception strategy detects malicious authorization to EOAs, malicious ownership changes, malicious transfer-address changes, and transfers to similar addresses.
OKX's wallet transfer guide shows confirmation details for recipient, amount, token/network, and network fee before completing a send.
OKX's Web3 Security White Paper says the OKX Web3 ecosystem, including the wallet, uses Blockaid for transaction simulation and verification, token security, and URL screening.
OKX Onchain OS wallet API documentation describes simulating blockchain transactions before execution to show expected outcomes and potential risks for Swap and Approve requests.
OKX Wallet launched full historical approval analysis, allowing users to view and manage approval records on the wallet homepage Approval tab.
OKX later enhanced approval management to view past approvals and filter malicious approval poisoning.
OKX documents adding a custom RPC endpoint in OKX Wallet on both the app and web extension; users enter network name, RPC URL, chain ID, currency symbol, and optional explorer URL.
OKX Wallet publishes a browser extension through the Chrome Web Store.
Chrome for Developers states that all Chrome Web Store extensions are signed by Google, with signing handled automatically when a package is uploaded.
OKX Wallet is recorded as source-unavailable proprietary software; no public source tree or reproducible-build instructions are published for independently reproducing the wallet release artifact.
